fixes.correction: Every figure is a Nair nobleman: men only, with topknots or front tufts and moustaches or grey stubble, no jewelled hair ornaments, no drop earrings and no saree-like drapes, so that no figure can be read as a woman. Make the gap the subject: the front rank stands as one straight shoulder-to-shoulder line of men across the middle of the frame, seen from behind and a little above, and exactly one person-width space in that line stands empty, bare polished stone with a single lamp's flame reflected in it. The floor beyond the line is darker and less mirror-bright, so that one reflection reads clearly and the space does not look like an open aisle. At the far end the sanctum doors show only fragments of gold and shadow, never a whole standing idol or any complete figure of the god. Keep the rain-silvered outer doorway at upper left, the carved granite pillars, the brass open-wick lamps and the warm night light, and leave the dark upper wall and pillar area clear for two captions.
fixes.issues: Only candidate v01 fails the beat and the setting. (1) The script's single gap in the front rank is not shown: the nobles are bunched into left and right groups around a huge open floor full of reflections, which reads as the aisle (the aisle the king later walks in 1.5), not one empty place in a rank with a single lamp's reflection. (2) The foreground figure at lower right reads as a woman (jewelled ornament in the hair bun, drop earrings, saree-like red-bordered drape). That clashes with an all-male rank and with the Padmini caption, since Padmini is meant to be absent. (3) The sanctum doors show a whole standing golden idol, which breaks 'the god is never shown whole' and contradicts the reclining Padmanabha in fragments on page 2. Note for the page: the nobles stand in 1.1 and 1.2 but sit in 1.3 to 1.5.

fixes.correction: Only Nagoji may have a thick curled moustache, grey at the temples, curly hair in a topknot and a gold ear stud: draw him exactly once, and make every other man clearly different. Stage it from in front of the back rows, looking toward the rear of the hall, with the open outer doorway and its silver monsoon rain behind him. Nagoji sits at the back among the lesser officers, facing the viewer in three-quarter view, face composed and eyes forward: Kerala topknot tied on the crown with grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and jaw, a tiny flush gold stud on the earlobe, the silver chain of office plainly visible across his bare chest, cream mundu and shoulder cloth. In the foreground is the rank ahead of him, seen from behind and a little to the side. In that rank, exactly two nobles turn their heads back over their shoulders and glance sidelong at Nagoji, with their eyes on him, not on the viewer. One is a heavy older man with a shaven head, a small front tuft and heavy gold ear-rings; the other is a thin younger man with his hair loose and no moustache. Everyone else faces forward. Keep the seated rows on the polished, lamp-reflecting floor, the brass open-wick lamps and the dark carved pillars, and leave the dark ceiling and upper pillar area clear for two captions.
fixes.issues: Only candidate v01 fails. The two nobles beside Nagoji are near-copies of him: thick curled moustaches, grey at the temples, curly topknots and gold ear studs. That breaks 'draw each named person once, with no doubles', and the reader cannot tell which man is Nagoji. The beat is also wrong: the two nobles sit in the same row as Nagoji, not the rank ahead, and all three, Nagoji included, look back over their shoulders at the viewer instead of the nobles glancing sidelong at him. Nagoji himself (curly hair up with grey temples, moustache, clean chin, ear stud, silver chain, cream mundu and shoulder cloth) and the setting (rain doorway, lamps, polished floor) are good.

fixes.correction: Keep the low camera on the polished, reflecting granite floor, the receding carved granite pillars and brass lamp stands, the open outer doorway at left showing monsoon rain, the row of chanting priests on the low granite platform before the gold sanctum doors (chief priest in the centre facing us), and Varma seen from behind with his grey low knot, bare back, sacred thread and plain white mundu. Fix three things. (1) The hall is NOT empty: line both sides of the aisle with dense, silent ranks of bare-chested nobles in white mundus and shoulder cloths, seated and standing as on the previous page, leaving only a narrow open aisle of floor down the middle. (2) Varma must read small and alone between those ranks: place him in the middle distance, walking away from the camera down the empty aisle, no more than about a third of the frame height, not a large foreground figure. (3) He carries the same bare sword as on page 1: a naked steel blade with a red silk-wrapped hilt, resting flat across both upturned open palms held before him, with no scabbard and no fists gripping it. Varma wears no earring and no jewel of any kind. Keep the upper quarter of the frame (dark ceiling beams and shadowed pillar tops) free of heads and hands for two captions.
fixes.issues: v01 shows an EMPTY mandapa: none of the silent ranks of nobles the script calls for, so it contradicts page 1 (1.5 has the hall packed on both sides) and 2.4, where the nobles stand behind him. Varma is a large foreground figure, not small between the ranks. He grips a dark scabbarded sword in his fists, but 1.5 and 2.5 show a bare steel blade with a red silk-wrapped hilt resting flat across his palms. A small pearl earring shows at his ear, though the bible says no jewels. What works: the grey low knot, the sacred thread, the reflecting floor, the lamps, the priests at the far end and the rain through the outer doorway.

fixes.correction: Keep everything that works: Varma from behind at the sanctum threshold, dwarfed by the gold door leaves, with his grey low knot, bare back with the sacred thread and plain white mundu; the reverent fragments of Lord Padmanabha through the doors (rising serpent hoods, a vast resting hand, gold ornament, no face); the brass lamps, the reflecting granite floor and the rain glimpsed through a far doorway at left. Fix the missing prop: Varma still carries the dedication sword, and his hands must NOT hang empty at his sides. His elbows are bent forward and he holds the bare sword flat across both upturned palms in front of his waist, so that from behind the naked steel blade tip shows past one hip and the red silk-wrapped hilt shows past the other, the blade level with the floor. Keep the upper-left area of shadowed pillars and ceiling clear of figures for one caption.
fixes.issues: Continuity break: Varma stands at the threshold with both arms hanging at his sides and his hands visibly empty. He carries the sword in 2.1 and lays it down in 2.5, so it cannot vanish here. Everything else works: the back view, grey low knot, sacred thread, plain mundu, the gold doors, the reverent fragments of the reclining god and serpent hoods with no face shown, the lamps and the reflecting floor.

fixes.correction: Keep the kneeling figure on the reflecting stone before the threshold, the bowed head with the grey low knot, the aged varma-v1 face with thick moustache, the bare torso with the sacred thread, the plain white mundu, the still nobles standing behind at left, the near-foreground brass lamp with its bending flame, and the dark ceiling space at upper centre for the caption. Fix the missing prop: his hands are NOT flat on the floor and NOT empty. He kneels with his head bowed, holding the bare sword flat across both upturned open palms at knee height in front of him: naked steel blade pointing toward the sanctum, red silk-wrapped hilt nearest himself, not yet laid down (the next panel lays it on the stone). Varma wears no ear stud, earring or jewel of any kind.
fixes.issues: Continuity break: Varma kneels with both palms flat on the floor and no sword anywhere, yet in the very next panel (2.5) his hands lower the sword to the stone. A tiny ear stud shows on his ear, though the bible says no jewels. Otherwise strong: the bowed aged face with moustache, the grey low knot, the sacred thread, the plain mundu, the still nobles behind, the bending lamp flame in the foreground, and dark ceiling space for the caption.

fixes.correction: Composition correction: this is a closer two-shot of the whispering chief and his young neighbour, not of Nagoji. Do not show Nagoji's face. Show only a narrow sliver of his bare shoulder with the silver chain of office lying across it, cut off by the LEFT edge of the frame and filling no more than one tenth of the width. Centre-left is the heavy-set older chief (shaven head with a small tuft at the FRONT, heavy gold hoop ear-rings, red-bordered shoulder cloth, grey stubble, no thick moustache). He still leans to the right toward his neighbour, one hand cupped beside his mouth, eyes wide. On the right is the neighbour, younger and thin, with loose curly black hair and a plain cream shoulder cloth. His face is turned three-quarter toward the viewer and his lips twitch, pressed together and not smiling. All three men are STANDING side by side at the back of the hall facing the sanctum, exactly as in panel 3.4, never seated. Keep the same mandapa: carved granite pillars, brass open-wick lamps, the wet granite floor reflecting the flames and the rain-filled outer doorway at upper left. Keep the dark upper band above their heads clear for two balloons.
fixes.issues: v01 misses the script beat and breaks continuity with 3.4. Nagoji's full face fills the left half instead of only his shoulder and chain at the left edge. The young neighbour is missing, so the chief whispers to Nagoji. Both men are seated, although they stand in 3.4. The silver chain of office is not visible.

fixes.correction: Keep the hand-off of the coir-bound bundle of thin brown coconut-leaf ribs (no wooden pole, tips worn ragged) against the dark lamplit stone floor, but make it a true tight inset: frame at chest height and below so that NO face is in the picture. Show only the attendant's slim young bare forearms and hands reaching in from the left and the king's older, broader hands and forearms closing on the bundle from the right, with the white sacred thread visible across the king's bare chest and the top of his plain white mundu at the waist. If any part of the king's face does enter the frame, it must be the varma-v1 face from his attached sheet, aged, with his thick curled moustache under the nose and grey hair in a low knot at the back of the head, never a clean-shaven upper lip. The attendant is bare-chested in a plain short white mundu with no gold border and no shoulder cloth.
fixes.issues: The only candidate, v01, fails the principal's identity: the king receiving the broom has NO moustache, a clean upper lip and a different face, so he does not read as varma-v1. Every neighbouring panel gives Varma his thick curled moustache. The panel prompt attaches no reference sheet, which is likely why the face drifted. Also, the attendant wears a long gold-bordered mundu with a shoulder cloth instead of a plain short mundu with a bare chest, and the frame is a medium shot on Varma's face, not a tight inset on the hand-off. The broom itself is good: coir-bound ribs, no pole, ragged tips, hands sound.

fixes.correction: Draw Revathi Bayi ALONE: no other person anywhere in the frame, with no man, guard or figure in the background, in a doorway or at the frame edge. Nagoji stands off-panel to frame right and must not appear at all. Frame her from the waist up or closer, at frame left or centre-left. Her body stays angled toward the gatehouse, and only her head turns over her shoulder toward frame right, where he is. Her face is weary and drained, with no anger, and her eyes are level. Keep what worked in the last attempt: deep indigo sari with gold zari, long braid with jasmine, flat-coin necklace with the tali on its yellow thread, gold armlets and bangles, bell earrings, sandalwood line at the hairline, early-evening gold light, laterite courtyard walls and the red banner with a silver conch above the tiled gatehouse. Make the grey threading in her black hair clearly visible as a grey streak at the temple, matching the earlier panels. Leave open, low-detail evening sky across the upper middle and upper right of the frame for three short speech balloons.
fixes.issues: v01 shows a second figure at frame right: a man in a cream kurta and shoulder cloth with a maroon sash and sword, short loose hair with no topknot, and a stubbled beard. If he is meant to be Nagoji, his costume and beard are wrong, and the prompt says Nagoji is off-panel. Otherwise he is a stray bystander. Revathi's grey threading is also barely visible. Her weary turn of the head, costume and the courtyard are otherwise good.

fixes.correction: Keep the over-the-shoulder composition, the night rampart with distant fort lamps and camp lights, and Varma's grey low knot, bare shoulder and sacred thread at the right edge. Fix Nagoji to match the previous panel: gather his hair up into a neat Kerala topknot on the crown with clear grey streaks at both temples, with no long loose curls hanging to his shoulders. Shave his chin and jaw completely smooth, with no stubble, stipple or shadow. Keep the thick curled moustache and the tiny flush gold stud on the earlobe. Turn his body toward Varma in three-quarter front view so he faces him directly, not turned away and glancing back over his shoulder. Keep his face still and unreadable. Show the white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and the silver chain over the coat. Keep the upper-left and upper-centre night sky empty for three speech balloons.
fixes.issues: v01 fails Nagoji's chapter look and breaks continuity with 8.2 on the same page. He has no grey at the temples (the hair is all black), and the hair falls in long loose curls to the shoulders with only a small knot on top. The chin and jaw show visible grey stubble shading, not a clean-shaven chin. His body is also turned away from Varma, looking back over his shoulder, instead of facing him. The over-the-shoulder framing, white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain, ear stud, Varma's grey low knot and sacred thread, and the night rampart all work.

fixes.correction: Frame this as a tight close-up insert of the hands only: Varma's two aged, veined hands clenched on the top edge of the wet dark stone parapet, filling the lower two-thirds of the frame, knuckles pale and tendons standing out, with at most the forearms coming in from the frame edge. Show no face, head, back or full figure, and do not repeat the previous panel's over-the-shoulder view of the landscape. No rings or bracelets on his hands. Keep the night-after-rain light: rain beading on the dressed stone with warm glints from a small brass open-wick oil lamp, and a dark blue night beyond the parapet edge in the upper third, left plain and low-detail for the two balloons.
fixes.issues: Wrong framing: the script calls for a tight insert on his hands gripping the parapet, knuckles pale on wet stone. v01 is a medium over-the-shoulder shot of the whole leaning figure and landscape that largely repeats 9.1, so the beat is lost. Hands, setting and Varma's look are otherwise fine.

fixes.correction: Keep Varma exactly as drawn: profile against the night sky, grey low knot, sacred thread across his bare chest, plain white mundu, one hand lying open on the wet stone while the other loosens its grip. Push Nagoji much further back along the wall walk, about a third of Varma's height, soft-focus and blurred like a background figure, so Varma clearly dominates the panel. Nagoji keeps the white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain and Kerala topknot, with a touch of grey at the temples. His ear ornament is a tiny flush gold stud on the lobe with nothing hanging below it: no drop, ball, bead or pearl. Keep the upper sky plain and dark for the two balloons.
fixes.issues: Nagoji wears a hanging gold drop earring, clearly visible below the lobe. The author has ruled that it must be a small flush stud, enforced in selection. He is also drawn large and in sharp focus, not small and out of focus behind Varma as the script asks, and has no grey at the temples. Varma himself is good: profile against the sky, grey low knot, sacred thread, one hand open on the wet stone.

fixes.correction: Put the camera OUTSIDE the chapel in the evening forecourt, looking at the chapel's open doorway in local granite with a simple wooden cross above it, the same exterior and warm low light as the previous panel. Father Duarte is the focus, a mid-shot standing IN the open doorway, framed by the door, with the dim candlelit chapel interior (altar, front pew) behind him. Show his scholar's stoop, white-grey swept curly hair, and grey tired eyes looking out with quiet acceptance, not lowered. His callused, ink-stained hands are loosely clasped at his waist. He wears a plain black cassock with a plain black standing collar and a small cross on a thin chain, NO white collar tab. De Lannoy is OUTSIDE, in the near foreground at the left edge, in three-quarter back view: tall, pale grey hair tied with a black ribbon, worn white coat over a buff waistcoat, white breeches as in the previous panel. He has just stepped past the threshold, and Duarte stands behind him. Do NOT place De Lannoy inside the chapel or near the altar, and keep him smaller than Duarte in the frame. Leave the granite wall above the door and the sky at the upper left clear and low-detail for a caption and a speech balloon.
fixes.issues: Setting and continuity break. De Lannoy is drawn back INSIDE the chapel beside the altar, and Duarte stands in the doorway with the outdoor dusk behind him. In 10.2 De Lannoy has already stepped outside, and in 10.4 he is outside at the doorframe. So this panel flips the geometry: it reads as De Lannoy back inside and Duarte leaving, not Duarte in the doorway behind De Lannoy. De Lannoy also dominates the foreground in a mundu and sash, while the panel's subject (the caption is about Duarte's eyes) is small and in the midground. Duarte himself is on model: grey-white curls, no collar tab, ink-stained clasped hands, small cross.

fixes.correction: Keep this exact composition: the chapel doorway at evening with the altar, two lamps and the wooden cross behind; Nagoji at left in the white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain, hands behind his back, topknot with grey at the temples, tiny flush gold ear stud, looking down at the hand; Duarte at right, stooped, eyes lowered, his ink-stained right hand stopped in the air between them with the cassock sleeve fallen back from the wrist. Fix only the following. Duarte's cassock collar is a plain black standing collar closed all the way round the throat, black at its front opening, with no white tab, white notch or white linen showing anywhere at the neck. Nagoji's jaw and chin are smooth and clean-shaven, with no stubble shading.
fixes.issues: Strong composition and beat (Duarte's ink-stained, callused hand stopped between them, sleeve back from the wrist, Nagoji in white coat, red waistcoat, topknot, grey temples and a tiny flush gold stud, watching the hand). But Duarte's collar shows a white Roman-collar tab at its front notch (about x 0.77, y 0.37). It is visible even on the contact sheet, and it is the anachronism the script bans in every Duarte panel. With no lettering in this panel, nothing will cover it. Nagoji also has light stubble shading on the jaw.

fixes.correction: Show Duarte giving a blessing to another man, not crossing himself. Place Duarte in the right half of the frame, in the chapel doorway at evening, facing frame left toward Nagoji, who is just off-panel to the left. His eyes are open and rest on Nagoji with a calm, deliberate look. His callused, ink-stained right hand is raised in front of him at shoulder height, held away from his body, with the first two fingers extended together and the palm turned outward toward frame left, tracing the sign of the cross in the air toward Nagoji. The black cassock sleeve has fallen back from the wrist. The hand does not touch his own forehead, face or chest. His left hand hangs at his side. Use the same setting as the neighbouring panels: the stone chapel doorway in low warm evening light, with a plain altar under a white cloth, two brass lamps and a plain wooden cross on the wall behind. No figure on the cross and no crucifix on the altar. Keep his collar plain black and closed, with no white tab. Leave the upper-left area of plain stone wall or evening sky clear and low-detail for two speech balloons.
fixes.issues: Wrong beat. Duarte's eyes are closed and his ink-stained fingers press against his own forehead, so he reads as crossing himself or nursing a headache in grief, not blessing Nagoji. He stands inside the chapel turned away from where Nagoji would be. The altar also carries a figured crucifix, which goes against the plain-altar setting used in the other panels.

fixes.correction: Keep this composition: a wide evening strip with the stone chapel and its lit doorway at left, the fort wall and hill behind, and a clear band of evening sky across the upper part of the frame. Left to right: De Lannoy, Nagoji, Duarte, with De Lannoy's right hand gripping Nagoji's forearm. Fix Nagoji. His ear ornament is a tiny flush gold stud sitting on the lobe, with nothing hanging below it. His jaw and chin are smooth and clean-shaven with no stubble, and he keeps the thick curled moustache. His hair is gathered up into a Kerala topknot high on the crown, with only a few short curls at the nape, and shows first grey at the temples. Make the moment warm, not tense. The grip is a comradely clasp. De Lannoy looks earnest, with a faint steady smile. Nagoji listens with a softened face and turns toward him. Duarte stands beside them with a gentle, content look. Duarte keeps the plain black standing collar closed, with no white tab.
fixes.issues: Nagoji is off-model. His ear ornament is a gold ball hanging from the lobe, not the required tiny flush stud. His jaw and chin carry visible stubble. His hair falls in long loose curls around his shoulders with only a small bun, rather than the Kerala topknot, and shows no grey at the temples. The mood also reads as confrontation: De Lannoy grips Nagoji's arm with a hard frown and Nagoji glares back, which works against 'We are all servants now'. The composition, left-to-right order, chapel, fort wall and sky band are all good.

fixes.correction: Nagoji's ear ornament must be a tiny flush gold stud set directly ON the earlobe, no bigger than a lentil, with nothing hanging from it: no ball, bead, drop or ring below the lobe (the previous attempt copied the hanging gold drop from the reference sheet; do not). His chin, jaw and cheeks are smooth and fully clean-shaven, with no grey stubble or beard shadow; the only facial hair is the thick curled grey-and-black moustache. Keep everything else exactly as before: the dusk laterite rampart with the storm and rain far out over the sea on the right, Nagoji on the right of centre leaning both forearms on the parapet in the gold-bordered white mundu draped over one shoulder with his grey-streaked topknot, the young round-faced clean-shaven officer in a white coat and red waistcoat beside him on the left, and open sky across the top of the frame for lettering.
fixes.issues: v01 (the only candidate) is otherwise strong: dusk star-fort rampart, storm over the sea on the right, Nagoji leaning on the parapet in the gold-bordered white mundu with a grey-streaked topknot, and a young, round-faced, clean-shaven officer in a white coat and red waistcoat beside him. The open sky is good for lettering. It fails on Nagoji's identity. His ear ornament is a round gold bead hanging below the lobe, which is the drop from the sheet and not the flush stud the author ruled on 2026-10-02. He also shows visible grey stubble across the chin and jaw, where the bible requires a clean-shaven chin outside captivity.
